title: NoiseTexture2d memory leak when changing parameters at runtime
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1] and v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]


### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

If you change parameters of a NoiseTexture2D's Noise property at runtime, the memory usage of the application will steadily increase. I am using Windows Task Manager to observe the memory usage. I only tested changing the following parameters every frame (Vsync enabled):

- offset
- color_ramp.offsets

In the MRP included below, I tested a variety of surface sizes to see if that had any impact on the rate of the leak. 

Amount of memory increase after 5 minutes of runtime:
- One 32x32 texture: 8MB
- One 128x128 texture: 10MB
- Eight 128x128 textures: 34MB
- One 512x256 texture: 5MB (memory usage jittered greatly, so this is approximate)
- One 512x512 texture: 6MB (memory usage jittered greatly, so this is approximate)

I tried statically disabling Mipmap generation and the seamless property. Neither had any effect on the leak rate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a TextureRect to a scene
2. Set the texture to a NoiseTexture2D
3. Set the Noise to FastNoiseLite
4. Add a script which changes some parameter (like offset) of the FastNoiseLite every frame. See below.
5. Run the scene
6. Use Task Manager to observe the allocated memory slowly increasing over time.

Here is an example script which can trigger the issue:

```gdscript
extends TextureRect

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    texture.noise.offset.x += delta * 10.0
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Here is a simple project which shows the issue. The main_scene has 8 instances of TextureRect in order to see the effect faster, but it will still repro with a single TextureRect.

[NoiseTextureMemoryLeak.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23194553/NoiseTextureMemoryLeak.zip)
